recipe.title: Creamy Chicken Poblano Skillet
recipe.summary: Air-fried chicken with a cauliflower-rice, black bean, and corn skillet topped with creamy poblano sauce and salsa verde protein chips.
recipe.story: The chicken cooks whole in the air fryer so it stays juicy while the skillet comes together on the stove. A measured creamy poblano topping and crunchy salsa verde chips finish each serving.
recipe.serving_size: 5 ounces skillet mixture, 3.75 ounces cooked chicken, 1/4 cup sauce, and 1/2 ounce protein chips
ingredients: 1 1/4 pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts, approximately 3 chicken breasts
1 cup drained and rinsed black beans
3/4 cup Herdez Roasted Poblano Salsa Cremosa
1/4 cup Chobani Nonfat Plain Greek Yogurt
2 ounces Simple Truth Salsa Verde Protein Tortilla Style Chips
instructions: Pat the whole chicken breasts dry. Rub them evenly with the olive oil, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Place the chicken breasts in the air-fryer basket without overlapping. Air-fry for 10 to 14 minutes, turning halfway through cooking.
Confirm that the thickest part of each chicken breast has reached 165°F before eating. Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
While the chicken cooks, lightly coat a large skillet with cooking spray and heat over medium-high heat.
Add the cauliflower rice and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until tender and the excess moisture has evaporated.
Stir in the black beans and corn. Season with salt and pepper and cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
Combine the poblano sauce and Greek yogurt in a microwave-safe bowl. Microwave for 30 seconds, stir, and microwave for another 15 seconds if needed.
For each serving, plate 5 ounces of the skillet mixture with 3.75 ounces sliced cooked chicken, 1/4 cup creamy poblano sauce, and 1/2 ounce crushed salsa verde protein chips.
tips: Keep the chicken breasts whole during cooking and slice only after the 5-minute rest.
Weigh the cooked skillet mixture during taste testing to confirm the 20-ounce finished yield before final nutrition publication.
Keep the protein chips separate until serving so they stay crunchy.
